references.text: Paul quotes directly from Deuteronomy 30:14 in Romans to explain righteousness by faith. He uses the words 'the word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart' to show that salvation by faith is available to all.
The psalmist describes how he hides God's word in his heart, which connects to the idea that the word should be in the heart to keep it.
Jeremiah prophesies about the new covenant where God will put His law within them and write it on their hearts. This expands the concept that the word should be in the heart.
Ezekiel speaks of God giving the people a new heart and a new spirit, so they can follow His commands. This relates to the idea that the word must be in the heart to obey it.
The mouth of the righteous speaks wisdom, and his God's law is in his heart. This reflects the thought that the word is in the mouth and in the heart.
The wisdom of binding words around the neck and writing them on the tablet of the heart connects to the idea that God's word should be near, in the heart.
